Sugar Skulls (Calaveras de Azúcar)

Served at: Dia de los Angelitos

Makes 6-8 medium skullsPrep 30 min

Sugar Skulls, or Calaveras de Azúcar, are iconic decorations for Dia de los Muertos, particularly significant during Dia de los Angelitos (November 1st), when they honor deceased children. These sweet, edible (though often purely decorative) confections symbolize life, death, and remembrance, bringing a touch of festive artistry to altars and celebrations.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (800 g) granulated sugar
  • 4 teaspoons meringue powder (for skulls)
  • 4 teaspoons water (for skulls)
  • 2 cups (240 g) powdered sugar (confectioners' sugar)
  • 2 tablespoons meringue powder (for royal icing)
  • 4-5 tablespoons water, or as needed (for royal icing)
  • Food coloring gels
  • Edible glitter, edible sequins, small candies (optional, for decoration)

Method

  1. In a large bowl, combine the granulated sugar and 4 teaspoons of meringue powder. Mix thoroughly with your hands or a spoon until well incorporated.
  2. Gradually add 4 teaspoons of water, mixing continuously. The mixture should feel like damp sand and hold its shape when squeezed, but not be too wet or sticky. Adjust water by drops if needed.
  3. Firmly press the sugar mixture into your skull molds, ensuring there are no air pockets. For two-piece molds, fill both halves. For one-piece molds, fill and level the back.
  4. Carefully unmold the sugar skulls onto a parchment-lined baking sheet or flat surface. If using two-piece molds, gently press the two halves together to form a full skull.
  5. Allow the sugar skulls to air dry completely for at least 8-12 hours, or up to 24 hours, depending on humidity. They should be hard to the touch.
  6. While the skulls dry, prepare the royal icing. In a medium bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar and 2 tablespoons of meringue powder.
  7. Gradually add water, one tablespoon at a time, mixing until the icing is smooth, thick, and holds its shape but is still pipeable. Divide the icing into separate bowls and tint with food coloring as desired.
  8. Transfer the colored icing to piping bags fitted with small round tips, or use zip-top bags with a tiny corner snipped off.
  9. Once the sugar skulls are completely dry and hard, decorate them with the royal icing, creating intricate patterns, eyes, noses, and mouths. Use edible glitter, sequins, or small candies to add extra sparkle and detail.
  10. Allow the royal icing to dry and harden for several hours before handling or displaying the decorated sugar skulls.

Tips

  • Drying time is crucial for sturdy skulls; do not rush this step. High humidity can prolong drying.
  • Meringue powder is essential for binding the sugar and creating durable skulls and icing. Do not substitute.
  • These sugar skulls are primarily for decoration and symbolic offerings, not typically for eating due to their hardness and high sugar content.
